points.title: Validation definition
points.must: An automatic check by the computer that data is sensible / reasonable and follows the rules; cannot check data is correct.

points.title: Verification and its methods
points.must: A check that data was entered / copied accurately and matches the original source; Double entry (typed twice, compared) and visual check / proofreading against the original document.

points.title: Validation vs verification comparison
points.must: Table: question asked, who does it, examples, and an error each one catches (150 vs 67 typed as 76).

points.title: Validation checks
points.must: Presence, type, range, length, lookup, format, uniqueness — each with a rule example.

points.title: Validation in SQL
points.must: NOT NULL, the data type, CHECK (… BETWEEN …), CHECK (… IN (…)), CHECK (LENGTH(…) = n), LIKE pattern, UNIQUE — in a CREATE TABLE.

points.title: Worked validation example
points.must: A scenario (e.g. olympiad registration) with each check named as validation or verification and why.

points.title: ORDER BY, ASC and DESC
points.must: ORDER BY sorts the rows of the result; ASC (default) or DESC; always the last clause; Numbers small → large, text A → Z, dates oldest first for ASC; reverse for DESC; typical task wording.

points.title: ORDER BY examples
points.must: Sorting by one field ASC and DESC, and by two fields (second field decides ties); WHERE before ORDER BY.

points.title: Order of clauses
points.must: SELECT → FROM → WHERE → GROUP BY → ORDER BY.

points.title: Aggregate functions
points.must: COUNT(*), SUM, AVG, MAX, MIN (and GROUP BY) with an example and its result.

points.title: Join definition
points.must: A query that combines rows from related tables by matching the foreign key with the primary key.

points.title: Join condition
points.must: WHERE Table1.FK = Table2.PK (or JOIN … ON …) — with the Titles / Publishers example.

points.title: Two ways to join
points.must: FROM A, B WHERE A.x = B.x and FROM A JOIN B ON A.x = B.x give the same result.

points.title: Steps for a join query
points.must: Fields as Table.field → both tables in FROM → join condition → extra conditions with AND → ORDER BY last; A query with two join conditions (tables − 1), e.g. student name, book title, loan date.

points.title: Worked join example
points.must: A join with an extra condition and ORDER BY, plus its result table (e.g. books published in Almaty, cheapest first).

points.title: Missing join condition
points.must: Without it every row is paired with every row (5 × 3 = 15 rows) — a meaningless result.

points.title: Table.field and aliases
points.must: A field that exists in both tables must be written with the table name; aliases t, p.

points.title: Database with multiple tables
points.must: Data about different entities in separate tables linked by keys; each fact stored once, less redundancy.

points.title: Primary key vs foreign key
points.must: PK uniquely identifies records of its own table, never NULL; FK links to the PK of another table, can repeat.

points.title: Building the tables with FOREIGN KEY
points.must: From the ERD: tables, fields, PKs; FK in the 'many' table; same type as the PK; create parent tables first, then child tables; insert parents first; A full example: FOREIGN KEY (StudentID) REFERENCES Students(StudentID) in Loans.
